idea: Set in a plain engraved serif, centered like a chart legend: 'HERE BE DRAGONS' struck through with a single clean rule, and beneath it in small caps 'Here be unmeasured coastline.' A cartographer's joke turned honest: the monsters were just the edge of what anyone had surveyed.

A longitude table typeset like a ship's logbook page: 'Longitude, 1714–1761' with rows of prize, claimant and error in minutes, ending with the line 'Harrison: 5 seconds in 81 days.' For people who love a story where the clock beat the astronomers.
The word 'LATITUDE' set large, with 'LONGITUDE' beneath it in the same size and a bracket noting 'one was easy.' A quiet nerd joke about why one coordinate took until the 18th century.

A compass rose built entirely from letters: the 32 points of the wind spelled out (N, NbE, NNE, NEbN...) as a radial text wheel, with no drawn lines at all. Looks like an ornament from afar and reveals itself as vocabulary up close.

Place names that are apologies, set as a gazetteer list: 'Cape Tribulation, Mount Misery, Disappointment Island, Point Hicks Wasn't, Useless Loop, Cape Farewell.' Explorers naming things in a bad mood; a list that reads like a poem.

Tiny type in a column, like a map index: 'You are here' repeated down the shirt front in decreasing size until the last one is a single dot. A dry joke about location, scale and where you actually are.
The word 'TERRA INCOGNITA' in spaced Roman capitals, with the lower line 'Updated daily, for now.' Gives the old blank-map phrase a modern shrug about how much is still unknown.

A dead-reckoning formula as a typographic poster: 'Speed × Time + Heading = Probably Here' set in a chart-label serif with a small X. Honest about navigation before satellites, and applicable to life.

The names of the 1768-1779 Cook voyage's 'unknown' coastlines replaced by the single legend line 'Charted from memory, corrected by rocks.' Set as a map cartouche in pure type, with ruled border. For the sailor who learned the hard way.

Meridian Wars: a column of every prime meridian once used (Paris, Ferro, Greenwich, Washington, Pulkovo, Cádiz...) typeset as a ranked list, with Greenwich circled in a lettered ring and the line 'Agreed in 1884, 22 to 1.' For people who like arguments settled by vote.

'The map is not the territory' reworked as lettering where the word TERRITORY is set in huge type and the word 'map' sits tiny in the corner, pointing at it with a hairline arrow. Korzybski in two sizes of type.
A tide-table layout reading 'HIGH 04:12 / LOW 10:31 / HIGH 16:40 / LOW 22:55' and below, 'Nothing else is scheduled.' Calm, nautical and quietly a manifesto for doing little.
'Sounding' set vertically, a depth-chart lettering exercise: numbers in fathoms descend down the shirt in tiny type, ending at the bold word 'NO BOTTOM.' The old lead-line report as a mood.

Nautical signal flag alphabet rendered in one ink as pure geometric type blocks code-drawn, spelling 'ALL HANDS' decoded in small letters beneath. Readable to anyone who looks closely, which is the point.
The old atlas phrase 'Scale of Miles' set with a ruler bar whose units are wrong on purpose: '0 — 1 — 2 — Several.' For anyone who has trusted a hiking estimate.

Stacked lettering of ship names that vanished and were found: 'Erebus. Terror. Endurance. Shackleton found it in 2022.' with each year set as a small caption. A memorial that makes people ask about the ships.
'Magnetic north moves 55 km a year. Keep checking.' set as a small label like an instrument plate, in a rounded rectangle, plain black type. A quiet piece of advice disguised as a fact.

Spelling variants of one city across old atlases, stacked and fading: 'Constantinople / Istanbul / Stamboul / Kostantiniyye / Byzantium', the last line bold. A shirt about names being the oldest map projection.

'Mercator was right about the lines. Everyone else was wrong about Greenland.' set in a title-page serif with a tiny code-drawn Greenland-sized rectangle. A map-nerd's conversation starter that is fair to Mercator.

A survey benchmark disc recreated purely in type: ring text 'U.S. COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY — FOR INFORMATION WRITE TO DIRECTOR — $250 FINE OR IMPRISONMENT FOR DISTURBING THIS MARK', with 'ELEV. 0000' in the centre. A real, strange public warning that surveyors will love.
